text:
Predicates:
Allowed(x, y) ::: x is allowed to move in with y.
ManagedBuilding(x) ::: x is a managed building.
Pet(x) ::: x is a pet.
Cat(x) ::: x is a cat.
Deposit(x, y) ::: x requires a deposit of y.
SecurityDeposit(x, y) ::: x has a security deposit of y.
MonthlyRent(x, y) ::: x has a monthly rent of y.
More(x, y) ::: x is more than y.
Rent(x, y) ::: x rents an apartment in y.
Premises:
∃x (ManagedBuilding(x) ∧ Allowed(pet, x)) ::: Pets are allowed in some managed buildings.
∀x (ManagedBuilding(x) → Deposit(x, securityDeposit)) ::: A deposit is required to rent an apartment in a managed building.
∀x (SecurityDeposit(x, y) → (y = monthlyRent ∨ More(y, monthlyRent))) ::: The security deposit can be either equal to the monthly rent at a managed building or more.
Cat(fluffy) ∧ Cat(fluffy) ::: Fluffy is Tom's cat. Cats are pets.
ManagedBuilding(oliveGarden) ::: The Olive Garden is a managed building.
MonthlyRent(oliveGarden, $2000) ::: The monthly rent at the Olive Garden is $2000.
More($2000, $1500) ::: $2000 is more than $1500.
(Rent(tom, x) ↔ (Allowed(tom, fluffy) ∧ More(securityDeposit, $1500))) ::: Tom will rent an apartment in a managed building if he is allowed to move in with Fluffy, and the security deposit is no more than $1500.
∀x (ManagedBuilding(x) ∧ Allowed(pet, x) → Allowed(person, pet)) ::: If a managed building allows pets, then people are allowed to move in with a pet.
Conclusion:
Allowed(tom, fluffy) ::: Tom is allowed to move into an apartment in The Olive Garden with Fluffy.
